institutionName: Western Norway University of Applied Sciences (HVL)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Norway offers a very unique type of education in friluftsliv, in no other country is it possible to study friluftsliv at a university level. Friluftsliv differs from other outdoor education in its core philosophy. The possibility to friluftsliv was my main motivation to go abroad.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it easy enough, there was always the option to call or email someone who could help, but in can take quite some time to find the information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive any when I arrived, and didn't need any, but before arriving I had good help from nice people at HVL over an online communication.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy, the place is very small and everything is in walking distance. I found housing through a student organisation which has multiple housing offers (Samam).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's almost like living on campus in such small town, very nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It starts quite easy with a great overview of the opportunities, but filling in all the right information can be tricky since all the universities does everything a little different it can be hard to get the answer on how you do it correctly for just yours.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could email the exchange office and a single info meeting you should sign up for.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got it just as I wanted, but I also had the great opportunity to sign up for an exchange student package at HVL.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It takes time and you might have to read a lot information and still re-do when get new information but it's worth it. I also felt it was easy to go a country cultural similar to my own (Norway/Denmark) through out the registration process.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found it very fitting.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I don't believe the education here can be compared to other place, the study of friluftsliv is very unique. The main thing we did was going multiple days trips in nature. It was excellent for this program, but I don't think that works for a lot of people other studies.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Outdoor leadership
Nature, culture and friluftsliv

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Outdoor leadership
Nature, culture and friluftsliv

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Studying friluftsliv can be very gear demanding, and almost everyone would have to invest in some new gear for the most pleasent experience.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I found a lot of the gear I needed I could buy cheaper here than back home.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The student organizations at HVL Sogndal did an amazing job. Lurkarlaget, Sjøspretten, studentspretten ect.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the student organisations and start climbing/bouldering.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
You will be surprised how many amazing places there are in Norway, way more than the once on social media. Some:
Sognefjellet 
Fjærland
Ervik
Hoddavik

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It's hard being in an international class, but through communities and student organizations. Say yes to all offers and try meet more through the once you meet.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Food

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The nature and the use and enjoyment of it.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Join student organizations 
Say yes to the offers you get 
Go explore

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: By applying to for housing at Saman on my own instead of through the system I got a solo room instead of a shared one, for a small extra fee.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The experience. The trips I been on and the things a have seen and tried.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Keep doing and finding the fun stuff when you feel homesick.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
